calls.title: Amar Bank & GrowthBook
calls.summary: The meeting centered on Amarbank's exploration of moving from Statsig to GrowthBook for their experimentation and feature flagging needs. With a current reliance on Statsig, which is hosted externally, Amarbank is concerned about data privacy following Statsig's acquisition by OpenAI. The team highlighted the necessity for self-hosted feature flags with enterprise-grade controls and a culture of experimentation. Discussions included the compatibility of GrowthBook with existing infrastructure, specifically integration with Google BigQuery, and the advanced statistical capabilities it offers. The trial period for GrowthBook is planned to run through July, with final decisions expected by the end of the month, taking into consideration pricing models and technical requirements.
calls.keywords: feature flagging, experimentation, self-hosted, data privacy, migration, pricing

calls.title: Amar Bank & GrowthBook POC Check in
calls.summary: Amar Bank's team explored self-hosting solutions for feature flags to comply with data sovereign and regulatory requirements. They considered GrowthBook for its robust BigQuery integration and appropriate pricing structure, as their existing Statsig license ends on August 31. Infrastructure costs posed a concern as estimates exceeded their budget. Discussions included the capabilities of SDKs for local evaluations and complex rollout rules, along with governance features for experimental oversight. The team also sought multi-ID support for enhanced accuracy in experiments, distinguishing their approach from Statsig's single-ID limitation. A sense of urgency surrounded the decision-making timeline, with plans for potential early legal and security reviews for a smooth transition.
calls.keywords: self-hosted feature flags, experiment setup, BigQuery integration, approval workflows, monitored ramp-up, cost estimation
